title: Liber Scivias
shelf_note: A medieval Latin manuscript of Hildegard's Scivias (Heidelberg, salX16 per the scan footer), shelved under Latin books. It fits.
rights_flag: The scan footer is burned in: "© Universitätsbibliothek Heidelberg" and "http://digi.ub.uni-heidelberg.de/diglit/salX16/0229". The work is a medieval manuscript and in the public domain. Only the digitisation's licence terms need checking; this is not a modern edition.
structure_note: pages_translated is 0 in the structure counts, but the book field says 400. One of the two counts is wrong. 32 printed backsteps and 90 repeats are what folio numbering produces: only rectos carry a pencilled folio number (this scan 229 = fol. 114), and versos inherit or misread it. I read these as foliation artefacts, not a splice.

pages.layout: Two columns of protogothic book hand with red initials 'I' and 'S'. Chapter numerals 'vi.' and 'vij.' sit in the right margin. A strip of the facing verso shows at the left edge.

missing.english: This is the one who is seen in the breast of the father described above.
missing.why: The sentence points back to a figure in Hildegard's vision. Without a note saying which vision image this is, a general reader cannot tell who 'the father described above' is.

book_verdict: The right leaf is in a fitting Scivias manuscript. The page has serious errors: a dropped negation ('non' read as 'ii') reverses the statement about angels and humans, and the facing page's edge strip is transcribed and translated as marginalia. Two clauses are also lost from the Isaiah passage and its gloss.
